terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the fare rules here, and try your methods from main.

tasks.title: Write childFare
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `FareRules.java`, below `main`, write a method called `childFare`. It takes one `int`, the single fare in pence, and gives back an `int`: half of it, in whole pence. Write all of it, from `static` to its closing brace.

Check calls `childFare` from code of its own with fares of its own, one of them odd, and reads what it gives back.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about the first line of a method.
Write the first line: `static`, the type it gives back, the name, and the parameter in round brackets.
In its braces, give back half of the parameter with `return`.
Take the `//` off the line in `main` that calls it, and run the program.
hints: A method goes inside the class but outside `main`: below `main`'s closing brace, under the Task 1 comment.
The first line has the shape `static <type it gives back> <name>(<type> <parameter name>)`. Inside, `return` gives a value back to whoever called it.
The method is `static int childFare(int singleFarePence) { return singleFarePence / 2; }`.

tasks.title: Write printTicket
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a `void` method called `printTicket`. It takes a `String`, the destination, then an `int`, the fare in pence, and prints one line:

```
Ticket to Corran, 320 pence
```

Check calls `printTicket` with destinations and fares of its own and reads the line it prints.
nextSteps: Write the first line: `void` in place of a type, because it gives nothing back.
Put the two parameters in the round brackets, in the order the task gives, separated by a comma.
Inside, print the line built from the two parameters.
Call it from `main` with a destination and a fare of your own.
hints: A `void` method does its job and gives nothing back, so it has no `return` with a value.
Parameters are written as type and name, one after another with commas: `(String destination, int farePence)`.
Inside, one line: `System.out.println("Ticket to " + destination + ", " + farePence + " pence");`.

tasks.title: Write partyFare
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a method called `partyFare`. It takes three `int`s: the adults, the children and the single fare in pence, and gives back an `int`: what the whole party pays. Each adult pays the single fare, and each child pays the child fare. Call `childFare` from Task 1 for a child's fare.

Check calls `partyFare` with parties and fares of its own, one fare odd, reads what it gives back, and reads your lines for the call to `childFare`.
nextSteps: Make sure Task 1 passes first: this method builds on it.
Write the first line with three parameters, in the order the task gives.
Work out the adults' part and the children's part, calling `childFare` for one child's fare.
Give back the two added together, and try it from `main`.
hints: One method can call another, just as `main` does: write its name and the value to pass in round brackets.
`childFare(singleFarePence)` is one child's fare. Multiply it by the number of children.
The return line has the shape `return adults * singleFarePence + children * childFare(singleFarePence);`.

tasks.title: Make seatsAfter give back the seats
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, Ossian's `seatsAfter` should take the passengers who board off the seats left, but in `main` `seatsLeft` never changes. Make it give back, as an `int`, the seats left after `boarding` passengers board, and never less than 0.

Check calls `seatsAfter` with seats and passengers of its own, one where more want to board than there are seats, and reads what it gives back.
nextSteps: Run the program: `main` prints 48 seats left after 5 board. Read the lesson's part about copies.
Change the type in front of the name, so the method gives back a number.
Give back the seats left, and 0 when more want to board than there are seats.
In `main`, keep what it gives back in `seatsLeft`, and run again.
hints: A method gets copies of the values it is called with. Changing a parameter changes only the copy, never the caller's variable.
To get a value out of a method, give it back with `return`, and have the caller keep it: `seatsLeft = seatsAfter(seatsLeft, 5);`.
The method is `static int seatsAfter(int seatsLeft, int boarding)`, with `if (boarding > seatsLeft) { return 0; }` and then `return seatsLeft - boarding;`.
